event_confirmation: Dell's own notice of 2026-11-10 (Business Wire, listed on StockTitan's DELL feed https://www.stocktitan.net/news/DELL/): Q3 FY27 call on Tuesday 2026-11-24 at 3:30 p.m. CST, with results and guidance released before the call. So the release is after the close (amc), as in every prior print. The German preview https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/dell-quartalszahlen-am-24-november-963689 (2026-11-16) says the same.
conviction_note: abs_move 12% (above the 8.57% event-implied move because realised vol is 131.8%, a full-year guide update is likely, and the last three prints moved +15.8/+32.8/+21.9) times p_up 60, which gives +2.4. The lean comes from a guide bar that Dell has cleared by 47-68% on EPS for two quarters, from counterparties that spoke after Dell and all point up (Nvidia, CoreWeave, SMCI, Lenovo ISG, Wistron) and from a 41% de-rating with no company news. It is held to 60 because the tape sold through Nvidia's beat on 11-17, PC units fell 25% against a +15% client guide, and the AI order comparison against $60.9B is hard. impact_sum (+3.6) is larger than the scaled number because the findings are sized one by one and several positives are independent counterparties, while p_up carries the macro risk that the AI trade sells any beat.
bar: Company guide for Q3 FY27: revenue $49.0B, non-GAAP EPS $6.50, AI server revenue $19B, infrastructure ~+145%, client ~+15% (8-K exhibit 99.1 of 2026-09-01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001571996/000157199626000039/exhibit991earnings8kq2fy27.htm, and the CFO blog https://www.dell.com/en-us/blog/record-results-reflect-compounding-advantages/). Street consensus $6.63 EPS on $50.63B with a $7.25 whisper (Earnings Whispers via finviz, 2026-11-16, https://finviz.com/news/423394/dell-must-prove-its-95-billion-ai-backlog-can-convert-despite-memory-constraints); a 2026-11-18 preview carries the same $6.63/$50.63B. FY27 guide $192B / $25.50 EPS / $74B AI servers, against consensus FY27 EPS $26.01 and FY28 $30.65 (TIKR, updated 2026-11-18). Read against the guide, the bar is sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest about 12.4M shares (~1.9% of shares outstanding, ~4% of float), 1.6-1.8 days to cover as of early November 2026 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dell/shortinterest; tapeboard puts it at 4.2% of float on 2026-09-30). Not crowded, so a squeeze is no reason to shrink a negative. Skew is +1.14 vol points (25d put minus call), close to flat; put/call OI 0.62; the baseline reads 'balanced'. The tape is the extreme part: -41.0% in 20 days, -8.3% in 5, 49.7% below the 52-week high, 20-day realised vol 131.8%. ATM straddle 12.94% to the 11-27 expiry, event-implied 8.57%.

findings.finding: Dell beat its own non-GAAP EPS guide by 47% in Q2 FY27 ($7.04 actual vs $4.80 guided) and by 68% in Q1 ($4.86 vs $2.90), and revenue by $2.5B (Q2: $47.0B vs $44-45B) and ~$8.6B (Q1: $43.8B vs $34.7-35.7B). The Q3 guide of $6.50 sits BELOW Q2's $7.04 actual on $2B more revenue, and consensus ($6.63 / $50.63B) is only 2% / 3.3% above that guide, so the bar is close to a guide that has been conservative twice running.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two beats above produced +32.76% (2026-05-28) and +15.81% (2026-09-01) in the baseline; the FY26 Q4 print +21.93%. In FY26 smaller beats produced -8.88% and -2.08%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected another guide-crushing quarter, consensus would sit well above $6.63 (the whisper is $7.25) and the stock would not be at ~11x forward EPS, down 41% in 20 days. Management warned that some Q2 mix and rate benefits will not repeat, and that is why the sell-side stayed near the guide.
findings.independence: Q1 history: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2185289/dell-technologies-delivers-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results (2026-05-28). The consensus and whisper come from a different source: https://finviz.com/news/423394/dell-must-prove-its-95-billion-ai-backlog-can-convert-despite-memory-constraints

findings.finding: Nvidia reported after Dell last spoke (2026-11-17, quarter to 2026-10-25, which overlaps Dell's Aug-Oct quarter almost exactly). Data center revenue was $107.6B, +21% q/q and +110% y/y, total revenue $115.8B against $109.1B consensus, Q4 guided to $130B ±3%, and Vera Rubin NVL72 called the 'fastest product ramp in its history'. Dell's own Q3 AI server guide is $19B, +16% q/q from $16.4B, below the GPU supplier's sequential growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell rose ~5% premarket on 2026-11-18 on Nvidia's print and a Citi preference call (https://finviz.com/news/424515/why-is-dell-technologies-stock-surging-today), then gave it back: $320.55 on 11-16 to $296.01 today.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Nvidia has been public for a week. What is not priced is the read-through to Dell's Q4 and FY guide. If it were, Dell would have held the 11-18 bounce rather than falling ~8% more in five sessions, and consensus FY27 EPS ($26.01) would sit further above the $25.50 guide.
findings.independence: Q4 guide and interim-CEO context from a different outlet: https://aiweekly.co/alerts/nvidia-q3-revenue-hits-1158b-up-103-data-center-1076b-guides-q4-to-130b

findings.finding: CoreWeave (Q3 to 2026-09-30, reported 2026-11-10) spent $14.5B of capex in the quarter, raised the low end of FY26 capex to $37-39B, and grew backlog 27% q/q to $132.5B. Bernstein estimates emerging AI clouds are about 27% of Dell's FY27 revenue, so this is direct evidence that this customer class kept buying through Dell's quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history; neocloud demand was the stated driver of the +32.8% (May) and +15.8% (Sept) reactions, both on AI orders and backlog.
findings.why_not_priced: The market's fear since November is neocloud credit and a Texas data center moratorium, not current demand. If CoreWeave's capex were in Dell's price, Dell would not have fallen 15% on 11-05 with 'nothing Dell has said this week' (TIKR) to justify it. It is not confirmed that CoreWeave is a Dell customer in this quarter, and it buys from several OEMs.
findings.independence: The 27% customer-mix estimate comes from Bernstein via TIKR: https://www.tikr.com/blog/dell-has-tumbled-since-september-why-bernstein-still-sees-103-upside

findings.finding: Lenovo's ISG (server) segment, Jul-Sep 2026, reported 2026-11-19: revenue +178% y/y to $11.3B and operating profit above $1B for the first time (~9% margin), with CSP revenue up ~170%. A direct peer selling the same Nvidia racks against the same memory inflation made money on AI servers in the months that overlap Dell's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell's ISG margin has been the debated line: 10.5% in Q1 FY27, 15.0% in Q2, against a mid-single-digit AI target. The Q2 margin surprise went with +15.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews (Earnings Whispers 11-16) frame memory as squeezing ISG margins and say management warned that Q2 benefits won't repeat. A peer's profitable AI quarter five days before the print has not moved Dell's consensus EPS off ~2% above guide.
findings.independence: Peer, not counterparty. Same company's release: https://via.tt.se/pressmeddelande/4648074/lenovo-group-q2-financial-results-202627?publisherId=259167

findings.finding: Super Micro (Jul-Sep quarter, reported 2026-11-03) delivered $19.9B of revenue against an original $14.5-15.5B guide, above even its own 10-20 prelim of $18.5-19.5B. It raised FY27 to $72-82B from $65-72B, at 12.7% gross margin. AI server shipments ran well ahead of guides in the peer set during the first two months of Dell's quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: n/a for Dell; SMCI itself +6% after hours on the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced as sector news. Dell fell 15% in the two sessions after SMCI's beat (11-04/11-05, midterm and Texas sell-off), so the market did not translate the peer's shipment surprise into Dell's numbers.
findings.independence: SMCI's own 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001375365/000137536526000026/exhibit991_20260930.htm. Peer, not counterparty.

findings.finding: Wistron, a Taiwan AI-server ODM, posted record August 2026 revenue of NT$460.1B (+166% y/y) and October revenue of NT$402.6B (+117.6% y/y, +5.7% m/m). Jan-Oct revenue was NT$3.29T, so Aug-Oct comes to ~NT$1.24T, well above the Jan-Jul monthly average (~NT$293B). The supply chain was shipping AI servers at record rates through Dell's Aug-Oct quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Taiwanese monthly sales are not part of the US preview set. The source does not name Dell as the customer, so it is an industry proxy only.
findings.independence: October figure: https://apps.digitimes.com/tag/wistron/001720.html. Proxy; Dell not named as the customer.

findings.finding: Positioning and de-rating: DELL is -41% in 20 sessions and 49.7% below its 52-week high ($588.40 close on 2026-09-17), on no company news. TIKR and Trefis put the falls on 11-05 (-15%), 11-13 (-7.2%) and 11-16 (-7.0%) down to the post-midterm tech sell-off, the Texas governor-elect's data center moratorium pledge (office from January) and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's 11-12 resignation. Meanwhile consensus FY28 EPS rose from $21.40 (June) to $30.65 and the forward P/E fell from 26x (August) to ~11x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dell's last three prints all paid strongly (+15.8, +32.8, +21.9). But the 11-18 bounce on Nvidia's beat failed within days, which shows the current tape selling AI-hardware good news.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding is that the de-rating is macro while estimates rose, so a clean beat plus a raised FY guide meets a low multiple. Sized small because rule 5 says an unexplained drawdown is not evidence, and the Nvidia bounce failed.

findings.finding: PC units fell much faster than Dell's client guide implies. IDC has Dell's Jul-Sep 2026 shipments at 7.6M, -25.0% y/y (Gartner: 7.58M, -25.4%), against -5.0% in Apr-Jun. Dell guided client revenue +15% y/y for Q3 (~$14.4B on FY26 Q3's ~$12.5B), which needs ASPs up roughly 50% y/y against ~26% implied in Q2 (+20% revenue on -5% units). IDC blames the early-2026 channel pull-in; Gartner blames DRAM-driven price hikes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CSG has not driven a Dell reaction in the recent prints; the moves have been on AI orders and backlog. CSG is ~29% of revenue and ~19% of segment operating income (Q2 FY27: $1.14B of $5.92B).
findings.why_not_priced: Previews focus on AI conversion and memory in ISG; none quotes the -25% unit figure against the +15% client guide. Net of the rest: a 10% CSG shortfall is ~$1.4B of revenue and ~$0.1B of operating income, which the AI server line can cover if it lands $1-2B above $19B. Hence sized small. It is also a third-party unit tracker against a company guide, and Dell's commercial mix and repricing could close the gap.

findings.finding: AI orders face a hard comparison. Q2 FY27 AI server orders were a record $60.9B, 2.5x Q1's $24.4B, and backlog rose from $51.3B to $95B in one quarter. Previews name 'AI backlog near $95B' as a test, so lumpy Q3 orders below Q3 shipments (~$19B+) would print a backlog decline for the first time in the ramp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Order and backlog surprises drove the +32.8% (Q1 orders and raise) and +15.8% (Q2 $60.9B) reactions; in FY26, prints where AI orders disappointed went with -8.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus models carry revenue but not orders, and the previews treat $95B as a floor. There is no company number on Q3 orders, so this is inference from the primary document's comparison and sized small.
findings.independence: Same 8-K as finding 1 (different line). The preview framing is at https://www.tikr.com/blog/dell-has-tumbled-since-september-why-bernstein-still-sees-103-upside

findings.finding: Cash quality: Q2 FY27 free cash flow was $986M against $4.1B of net income. Financing receivables rose to $20.4B at 2026-07-31 from $14.3B six months earlier, and first-half new financing was $10.3B against $4.0B a year earlier. Dell is funding customers' AI deployments through DFS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Weak Q2 FCF was reported alongside a +15.8% reaction, so the market has looked through it once.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the bear case (TIKR: 18x is hard to justify 'while Dell keeps expanding its lending'), but neocloud credit fear has grown since Q2. Asked what the money buys: customer AI deployments corroborated by the $95B backlog. So it is not distress, and it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: Memory keeps inflating into Dell's Q4 guide period. TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices +10-15% q/q in 4Q26 (15-20% including HBM) and server DIMM contracts up more than 10%, with suppliers holding bargaining power. This is the input to Dell's Q4 ISG and CSG margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 FY27 component inflation was revenue- and margin-accretive (Dell reprices daily; ISG margin rose to 15%) and the stock rose 15.8%. In FY26 the memory-margin fear went with -8.88% and -2.08%.
findings.why_not_priced: Widely discussed, so largely priced. The open question is whether Dell guides Q4 ISG margin below Q2's 15% ('benefits won't repeat'). Lenovo's ~9% ISG margin (finding 4) cuts the other way, which is why this is small.

outside_window.finding: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa promised a moratorium on all new data center approvals until the Legislature acts. She takes office in January 2027. Texas holds >25% of planned US data center capacity through 2030.
Dell's COO Jeff Clarke speaks at the UBS conference on 2026-12-01 and the CFO at Barclays on 2026-12-09 (Dell notice of 2026-11-18), the next management commentary after the print.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the positioning/de-rating finding; it is one of the macro causes of the drawdown, not a separate Dell line

baseline_tension: The skew is flat (+1.14) and does not oppose a long lean. The -41% 20-day run-up cuts both ways: it de-rated the stock to ~11x on macro while estimates rose, which supports a positive reaction to a beat, but the failed bounce after Nvidia's 11-17 beat says the tape is selling AI-hardware good news, and that keeps p_up at 60 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 4 (financing is a question): financing receivables and weak FCF fund customer AI deployments corroborated by the $95B backlog, so not distress; resized -1.0 to -0.3.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy, macro transmission): PC unit trackers are a third-party proxy against a company guide and a segment that is ~19% of operating income; resized -1.5 to -1.0. Wistron does not name Dell as its customer; resized +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the orders-comparison finding rests on inference with no Q3 order figure; resized -1.0 to -0.8.

Rules 1, 6 and 7 left the rest standing: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing consensus sources; Dell's own reaction history pays beats; short interest is low; skew is flat. p_up (60) and abs_move (12) unchanged, so expected_move_pct stays +2.4 while impact_sum rises from 2.4 to 3.6.
